executionPlan: Implemented the play-transition spec as a shell phase machine (hero, chrome-out, waiting, entering, game, leaving, returning) plus game-side entry and exit legs. Verified with headless Chrome 154 over CDP on an Apple M1 Pro GPU (not SwiftShader): per-frame rAF sampler, Page.startScreencast frames, readPixels per render, Fetch interception, heap and listener counters. Production build run in a copy of the tree. Several browser-found defects were fixed along the way (see summary).
summary: Milestone 2 is implemented: cinematic Play and Exit, inline loading strip with Cancel/Escape, pause/resume and tab-hide pause, failure dialogs, prefetch, and clean repeated cycles. Lint, tests (348 passed, 17 files) and the copy-tree build all exit 0, and / First Load JS is 125 kB. Browser runs (dev and production build) show no layout jump, T-pose or blank frame on Play and Exit. Weak spots: at exactly C+360 the title is still at about 14 percent opacity (it finishes and the chrome is removed at about C+410), and the Exit swap pair has a pose step of 1.9x its neighbours (under the 2x limit but close). I did not touch the clothing bake, avatar.glb, or QA findings F7 and F8.

criteria.criterion: The Play transition follows play-transition.md sections 2 and 3: page chrome (nav, hero text, buttons, talk button, hints) exits with the specified stagger and easing, the canvas goes full screen with no layout jump, the camera moves from hero framing to the follow position while the avatar turns and walks into the world, the HUD enters, and input is enabled at about 1.9 s after click in the warm case; a recorded frame sequence (DevTools protocol screencast or per-frame captures) at the spec checkpoints shows no hard cut, no blank or T-pose frame and no flash of the hero layout.
criteria.evidence: Production run (metrics-prod-warm.json, seq-prod-warm screencast of 222 frames, hover first, 1440x900 headless Chrome 154, Apple M1 Pro): section and #about rects constant (1 distinct each), scrollWidth constant 1430, canvas wrapper rect constant. Chrome fades monotonic with ease-in and stagger; status, gestures and nav are 0 at C+360 and the title was 0.14 at the row nearest C+360 (it started about 50 ms late), and the chrome is removed only when its transitions end, last chrome opacity 0, S at C+417. Camera: start (0,1.2,-16.9) fov 32, fov 36.3 at S+100 (moving), ends at the follow pose (fov 55). Avatar yaw pi at S, still pi at S+150, 0 by S+530. Walk starts S+514, 2.17 m by S+1500. HUD buttons first visible S+1030, opaque S+1280, hint opaque S+1780, entry done announced S+1530 (click to entry done 1948 ms). Held W at S+1550 moved the avatar 1.51 m. T-pose rows 0 (hand-above-hips probe), blank screencast frames 0, readPixels shows 0 empty renders (rp2.mjs). Pixel diff of the pair spanning the swap: avatar-column swap pair 5.9 vs median of 10 neighbours 3.5 (1.7x, under the 2x limit); the ground at S matches the stage colour exactly (5,7,7 to 5,7,7). rAF p95 17.6 ms, p99 18.4, max 21.1 ms. Scrolled start (300 px) metrics-prod-s300.json is equally clean. Not verified: spec timings are met at C+410 to C+420 rather than C+360 for S because S waits for the chrome transitions; the 1.9 s target is met (1.93 to 1.95 s).

criteria.evidence: pause.mjs: Escape and P pause (dialog, Resume focused), second press resumes, Resume click works, 30 frames per 500 ms while playing and 0 while paused, camera static while paused, key events during pause ignored. Activating another tab set document.hidden true and showed the Paused dialog with Resume; returning did not resume. Frameloop is driven through the Canvas frameloop prop because an imperative setFrameloop was undone by Canvas re-renders (found in browser, fixed). voice.mjs with fake media device and a loopback peer connection: status listening, mic track live, click to mic track ended 13 ms, peer connection closed, stays off after Exit. failures.mjs: blocked game chunk (message, Retry loads the game after unblocking, A6 confirmed), all clips blocked (Retry works), WebAssembly rejected (dialog with the message, Back restores hero, gestures and scroll work), WebGL unavailable (Play stays disabled, portfolio usable), context lost via WEBGL_lose_context (dialog Graphics were interrupted with Retry and Back, rendering stopped, Back restored the hero and the canvas works after restore). A dialog click bug (pointer-events inheritance from the overlay) was found in the browser and fixed. Retry after a runtime or context fault is covered by shell tests only (returns to hero and replays), not run in the browser.

assumptions: Evidence was taken on desktop headless Chrome 154 with a real GPU (Apple M1 Pro, ANGLE Metal, about 60 fps idle) and a dev server for most runs; the headline numbers were repeated against the production build on a second port.
The loading case was exercised by holding the game chunk and clips with Fetch interception, not Slow 3G throttling.
The 'warm' case is hover for 1.5 to 2.5 s first (fetch and shader pre-compile), then click; GO is then ready at about C+360 to C+420.
The HUD 'Energy cells n/3' counter and an Interact touch button were left out because the challenge and interactions arrive in M3 and M4; a fake counter would mislead.
Safe-area insets were verified with Emulation.setSafeAreaInsetsOverride (47 px top, 34 px bottom), not on a device.
app/layout.tsx, ASSETS.md and app/fonts/jetbrains-mono appeared in the worktree at 21:42 (self-hosted font change) while this stage was running; I did not author them and left them untouched.
decisionsProposed: Scroll lock is body position fixed plus overflow-y scroll on the root instead of overflow hidden with scrollbar-gutter stable: measured on classic scrollbars, root overflow hidden shifts the page 10 px even with gutter stable. The reverse restores styles and calls scrollTo.
Pause is a Canvas frameloop prop derived from the session; an imperative setFrameloop is silently undone by the Canvas on any re-render.

The game warms up in two places: world shader pre-compile on the first hover or focus on Play (fine pointer only), and a warm-up gate that waits for the chrome exit; the compile stalls the GPU process for about 300 ms and must never overlap the chrome exit.
The swap waits for the chrome's real CSS transitions (capped 300 ms beyond 360), so S is about C+410 to C+420; the spec's S = C+360 cuts a half-faded title on any frame that starts late.
World reveal fades material opacity (transparent materials at opacity 1), not colour: a dielectric ground still shows about 6 to 8 levels of specular at a grazing angle.
Exit swap holds rendering for two frames first, because the hero Avatar commits one frame after the lights and a render in between shows a bare stage.
Dialog lives in components/game/shell (not ui) because the failure dialog must work before the game chunk loads.
lessonsProposed: jsdom tests cannot catch CSS pointer-events inheritance or compositor blank frames; run a real-browser click and a readPixels-per-render probe for every overlay and every scene swap.
Check Canvas props before using imperative R3F setters: Canvas re-applies frameloop on every re-render.

A mixer does not rewrite a bone whose animated value is unchanged, so another mixer's stopAllAction leaves the bind pose on screen; rebuild the animator in a passive effect after the other owner's cleanup.
Compile cost belongs to the GPU process, so it freezes CSS animations too; schedule it away from any visible transition.
